text:
Maria: Heads up — I'm seeing elevated GPU attach failures and packet loss in us-west-2b. First noticed ~10:30 UTC. Not full outage, but pod attach latency spikes and ~2-3% packet drop to that AZ. I'm starting a soft cordon so we can shift noncritical workloads.
Joel: Got it. What's the failure mode? preemptions or NIC flaps?
Maria: NIC errors + a handful of preempts. Some nodes showing kernel logs: `mlx5: eth0 link down` repeatedly. NVMe unrelated so KV cache still warm on surviving nodes.
SRE Bot: Alert: GPU attach failures >= 3% in zone us-west-2b for 6m — incident_id INC-2024-345
Jen: Good to know. Plan: cordon the zone, graceful drain best-effort for long-running jobs, reroute inference traffic to other zones with lower latency preference. Avoid full instant kill.
Tim: On the routing side I'll bump weights for us-west-2a/c and enable cross-zone burst for Dedicated pools. Any concern about cold cache cost?
Maria: Cache warming is a concern. For latency-sensitive routes, we'll prefer pinned instances in other zones first. For background training/cheap queues, allow burst on shared capacity.
Joel: Commands ready:
```
rictl zone cordon --zone=us-west-2b --reason="nic-flap" --drain=false
rictl evacuate --zone=us-west-2b --selector='tier!=critical' --grace=300
```
I'll run them in 2m unless someone objects.
Jen: Do it. I'll watch job reschedules and make sure autoscaler doesn't overshoot.
Deploy Bot: Rolling policy applied: traffic shift to us-west-2a (60%), us-west-2c (30%), fallback (10%)
Tim: Also enabling model-variant fallback for large-gen routes to a 8-bit quantized variant temporarily to reduce attach contention.
Maria: Copy. After cordon I'll start draining noncritical GPU pods. If attach fails exceed 10% we escalate to full zonal freeze and take capacity offline.
Joel: Monitoring: dashboards pinned — latency, attach-fail-rate, packet-drop, node-restarts. Ping me if attach-rate trends upward.
Jen: Cost note: cross-zone egress will increase until warm caches stabilize — flagging to finance if we exceed forecast.
Maria: Thanks. I'll post updates here every 5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
